use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: C2 JU publishes air and surface surveillance tracks that meet the track reporting criteria for exchange of surveillance information and data usable in providing threat warning information among systems involved in joint operations.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Publish air and surface surveillance tracks satisfying the track reporting criteria for exchanging surveillance information and data usable for threat warning among systems in joint operations.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: C2 JU publishes one set of air and/or surface surveillance tracks that satisfies the applicable track reporting criteria, making that track data available for exchange with systems involved in joint operations.
scope_contract.start_boundary: C2 JU has air and surface surveillance tracks to publish and initiates publication of those tracks.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The air and surface surveillance tracks have been published in a form that meets the track reporting criteria for exchange of surveillance information usable in threat warning.
in_scope_actions: Reporting tracks that meet the track reporting criteria for surveillance information exchange
excluded_adjacent_actions: Generating threat warning information from published tracks
Consuming or further processing published tracks downstream
Administratively defining or maintaining the track reporting criteria
variant_dimensions: Air track publication versus surface track publication

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU has performed sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration for the air/surface tracks to be published.
The C2 JU has reporting responsibility (R²) for each track to be published.
The minimum 12-second wait before reporting air and surface tracks has elapsed.

The C2 JU initiates publication of air and surface surveillance tracks after it initially achieves Active status or returns to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, or when it changes a track's Environment/Category or an operator rejects a difference report regarding those categories.

The C2 JU initiates publication of air and/or surface surveillance tracks after it achieves Active status or returns to Active status from Inactive or TDS Failure, or after a track Environment/Category change or operator rejection of a category difference report.
The C2 JU performs sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration for the air and/or surface tracks before transmitting them.

During correlation checks, the C2 JU does not automatically correlate two tracks when local/remote data indicate an identity conflict, different current Mode II codes, both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, or either track has a Strength value greater than 1.
The C2 JU assumes R2 for a locally held air or surface track when it has not received a remote report on that track for approximately 40 seconds.
The C2 JU performs common tracking by sharing a common track number and coordinating R2 so that each tracked object is reported by one C2 JU while the other C2 JUs withhold their reports.

When the C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation by transmitting the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to correlate the two tracks; the message identifies the track number to be retained and the track number to be dropped.
The C2 JU waits at least 12 seconds before reporting air or surface tracks.

The C2 JU publishes the air/surface track report by transmitting the track identity, position extrapolated to the time of transmission for real-time tracks (non-real-time tracks identified with time tags and not extrapolated), course in degrees true north, and speed in data miles per hour ground speed.
Diverges from Step 2: The C2 JU may perform the reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration as either an automatic or a manual function.

Diverges from Step 3: If the position or other data in a PPLI meet the C2 JU's decorrelation criteria, the C2 JU decorrelates the PPLI and local track data, then initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number, reporting both the PPLI Track Number/Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field as 'No Statement'.
Diverges from Step 3: The C2 JU shall not inhibit correlation of two tracks when either track has its Strength field set to No Statement.

Diverges from Step 4: When a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, when a non-J2.0 PPLI arrives with NPS set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or when Geodetic Position Quality is set to 0, the C2 JU assumes R2 of the IU and reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG with Identity Friend, Track Number/Platform/Activity values from prior messages, and PPLI Track Number/Identity Indicator set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 4: When a J7.0 Drop Track message (ACT=0) is received on a locally held track, the C2 JU assumes R2 at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track, and reports the track with Identity Friend, Track Number/Platform/Activity values from prior messages, and PPLI Track Number/Identity Indicator set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 4: When the C2 JU receives a J2 PPLI message with NPS set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure from a JU that has R2 of a locally held track, it may assume R2 at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
Diverges from Step 4: A C2 JU without R2 for a nonreal-time track with the TQ field set to value 0 assumes R2 for that track when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report.
Diverges from Step 5: The C2 JU assumes R2 on a common track when its local TQ at the time of transmission exceeds the received TQ by 2 or more.

Diverges from Step 6: When the C2 JU, as a receiving IU, receives a J7.2 message with RV set to 3 (manually initiated correlation), it automatically accepts the requested correlation unless (1) the tracks are of different Environment/Category or have an existing E/C conflict, (2) one track is simulated and the other live, or (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.

Diverges from Step 6: When the C2 JU, as a receiving IU, desires to reverse a requested correlation, it originates a reverse correlation request when the RV field in the J7.2 message is set to value 0, which indicates that a reverse correlation request would be acceptable.
Diverges from Step 7: The C2 JU may override the minimum 12-second wait time for air/surface tracks when operational necessity requires a shorter wait time or none at all.

Diverges from Step 1: If the C2 JU has the capability to automatically initiate tracks for release to the interface without operator action and that automatic capability is active but must not be used, the C2 JU deactivates the automatic capability. Exit: return to Step 1 and continue publication without automatic initiation.

Diverges from Step 2: If received surveillance data or a J7.0 (ACT=1) message conflicts with locally held track data (e.g., Environment/Category, ID/Identity Amplifying Descriptor, or Exercise Indicator differences), the C2 JU alerts the operator for manual resolution as applicable, resolves an Environment/Category conflict before an ID conflict, and resolves the difference using the appropriate J7 message, operator procedure, or voice coordination. Exit: after resolution, return to Step 2.

Diverges from Step 3: If automatic correlation is blocked by an ID conflict or differing current Mode II code, the C2 JU may use its initialization parameter or operator-selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C2 IUs; in lieu of specific interface direction, the restriction remains active by default. Exit: if inhibition is enabled, return to Step 3 and continue automatic correlation.

Diverges from Step 3: If automatic correlation is prevented by the Step 3 restrictions, the C2 JU may perform manual correlation instead, because those restrictions do not apply to manual correlation. Exit: continue after manual correlation and return to Step 3.

Diverges from Step 5: If the C2 JU receives a remote track report for a real-time track whose Track Quality equals the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN, it relinquishes R² for that track. Exit: stop publishing that track and return to Step 5 for remaining tracks.

Diverges from Step 6: When the C2 JU is a receiving IU for a J7.2 Correlation message, it accepts the requested correlation unless prespecified conditions require or allow rejection; if it rejects the request, it transmits J7.2 with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection. Exit: return to Step 6 with the rejected correlation not applied.

Diverges from Step 6: If a reverse correlation request would be considered but the originating JU set the RV field to value 1 in the J7.2 message, that reverse correlation request would be rejected due to the originator's constraint. Exit: continue at Step 6 without applying a reverse correlation.

Diverges from Step 8: After the C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT=2) Change Data Order message, it rejects any received data on that track that differs during a 30-second lock-out period, except for ID data from the controlling unit of the track and for processing an Exercise Status Order. Exit: after the lock-out, return to Step 8 and publish using accepted data.
Diverges from Step 8: If the C2 JU receives a J7.0 (ACT=2) Change Data Order message containing an ID of Pending, it does not accept that order. Exit: return to Step 8 retaining current track data.

Diverges from Step 8: If the C2 JU does not implement the changed Environment/Category and has R² on the track, it ceases reporting the track and transmits a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message. Exit: stop publication of that track and continue with any remaining tracks.

After successful publication, the air and surface surveillance track data is available for exchange with systems involved in joint operations, with the track information as complete, accurate, and timely as possible, and with the proper rules for reporting a track followed.

The air and surface surveillance tracks have been transmitted to the interface with identity, position (extrapolated to the time of transmission for real-time tracks; time-tagged and not extrapolated for non-real-time tracks), course in degrees true north, and speed in data miles per hour ground speed.
The C2 JU has resolved all conflicts between locally derived information and interface-reported information for the published tracks.

The published track data is correlated and dual designation is minimized; where a dual designation was resolved, the C2 JU has transmitted a J7.2 Correlation message identifying the track number to be retained and the track number to be dropped.

The C2 JU has assumed R² for any uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks being reported and retains R² on a published track until it is relinquished in accordance with the R² rules or until the track is dropped.
